basic.title: Senior Software Engineer
basic.summary: Senior software engineer building production systems across distributed backend services, data-intensive applications, machine learning, cloud platforms, and user-facing products. Work spans search and ranking, predictive analytics, NLP, real-time data pipelines, APIs, interactive web applications, and the infrastructure needed to operate them reliably at scale. Currently focused on AI-enabled software for utility planning and operations, combining product engineering, geospatial and time-series data, predictive models, cloud-native services, and production observability.

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Build full-stack and AI capabilities across Trinnex's digital-twin portfolio, spanning LeadCAST (asset inventory and replacement planning), waterCAST (the AI digital twin for capacity and condition), and Capacity Planner.

Designed the scenario path behind waterCAST that fuses an operator's own inventory with physical models and field-reading history, so an engineer tests a growth scenario in the browser and gets back maps and constraint lists explainable enough to defend to a regulator.

Owned the integration platform feeding LeadCAST, replacing one-off per-deployment scripts with reusable connectors for Esri ArcGIS inventories and Bentley ProjectWise documents, plus the templates that standardise the next rollout.

Extended Capacity Planner with machine-learning prediction and risk scoring, promoting models through a versioned serving path with drift monitoring, and surfacing feature attributions so a planner can show an auditor why an asset was ranked where it was.
experience.notes: waterCAST and Capacity Planner are used as the Trinnex project anchor. Numeric impact figures and candidate-specific implementation details are synthetic test data for resume-generation testing unless independently verified. The role is intentionally positioned as broad production software engineering with AI/ML, data, product, and cloud depth rather than as a DevOps-only role.

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Built backend services for a biomedical knowledge-discovery platform that turned scientific literature into searchable evidence for pharmaceutical and biotech research teams.
Developed NLP pipelines for biomedical entity and relationship extraction, converting unstructured research text into structured gene, disease, target, and evidence records.
Implemented search and ranking workflows over extracted biomedical evidence, improving the path from a broad scientific query to the most relevant supporting literature.
Built data-processing pipelines that normalized and enriched large document collections before NLP inference, reducing malformed records and inconsistent downstream features.

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Built backend and data services supporting Zillow's property-search and valuation experiences, serving model-derived housing information across high-traffic consumer surfaces.

Implemented production serving paths for automated valuation outputs, separating expensive model computation from latency-sensitive consumer requests through precomputation, caching, and asynchronous refresh.
Built event-driven processing for new and updated listings so property changes reached downstream search, analytics, and predictive systems without waiting for full batch reloads.
Optimized high-volume service and database access paths through indexing, caching, profiling, and query redesign, reducing tail latency on property and search requests.

experience.title: Software Engineer
bullets: Built distributed components in the Google Search serving path, supporting retrieval and ranking of candidate results under interactive latency requirements at global request scale.
Developed large-scale MapReduce and Flume pipelines over search and web data used to refresh indexes and derive signals for retrieval and ranking workflows.
Optimized latency-sensitive RPC and data-access paths, diagnosing tail-latency regressions that propagated across dependent Search services.
Refined Borgmon alerting and failure detection for tier-1 services, reducing noisy pages and making genuine serving regressions easier for on-call engineers to isolate.

note: Final Rowland universal-corpus design. The source profile remains broad Senior Software Engineering rather than DevOps-first. Trinnex retains the complete 69-selector Deepankar baseline and adds 38 current-market/Rowland-relevant selectors for 107 selector families and 535 hidden bullets, all constrained to the waterCAST + Capacity Planner product universe. Deloitte retains the same universal baseline plus the applicable additions for 106 selector families and 530 hidden bullets; MCP is omitted there for tenure chronology. For Deloitte, no technology selector owns a client vertical: projects/shared.json selects the JD-relevant anonymized client engagement(s), while the hidden corpus contributes reusable technical implementation depth, debugging/performance texture, reliability/security/data controls, testing, observability, and production handoff patterns. Older Tellic, Zillow, and Google roles remain fixed. Candidate-specific implementations and quantitative impacts are synthetic/inferred resume-generation material unless independently verified before live use.
